claim: Among maximum \( (5,3) \) Chebyshev permutation arrays \(C\subseteq S_5\), where \(d_\infty(\pi,\sigma)=\max_{1\le i\le5}|\pi_i-\sigma_i|\) and the known optimum is \(P(5,3)=10\), there are exactly 192 labeled maximum arrays. Under the natural 240-element isometry subgroup generated by all coordinate permutations and the global value reversal \(x\mapsto6-x\), these 192 maxima split into exactly three orbits of sizes 24, 48, and 120, with stabilizer orders 10, 5, and 2. The three orbits are distinguished by their unordered pair-distance spectra: respectively \((N_3,N_4)=(30,15),(25,20),(28,17)\), where \(N_j\) counts codeword pairs at Chebyshev distance \(j\).
integrity: All census and symmetry numbers are recomputed by the bundled dependency-free verifier from the metric definition; the exact optimum \(P(5,3)=10\) is explicitly credited to prior work rather than claimed as new.
limitations: Finite classification for \(n=5\) only; the orbit statement uses the explicit coordinate-permutation times value-reversal subgroup and does not assert that this is the full compatibility-graph automorphism group.
title: Three symmetry types of maximum \((5,3)\) Chebyshev permutation arrays
